headline: Wipro grants junior and mid-level employees 180 days on the bench
hook: Six months on the bench at Wipro
summary: Wipro has diverged from its Indian IT peers by allowing junior and mid-level employees up to 180 days to find billable projects while on the bench. Traditional industry practice typically limits bench time much more strictly to protect margins. This policy shift affects internal cost structures and workforce utilization metrics for the company. Indian retail investors tracking IT stocks should note how this bench management strategy impacts operational margins compared to peers like TCS and Infosys.
why_it_matters: Wipro's margin pressure could rise compared to lean IT peers.
winners_losers: Wipro employees gain / Wipro margins hurt

headline: Over half of Nifty 500 stocks have fallen 20% from yearly highs
hook: Majority of Nifty 500 stocks in correction
summary: Indian equity markets are facing a sustained sell-off, with 56% of Nifty 500 constituents now trading at least 20% below their 52-week peaks. The decline is driven by persistent foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows, rising bond yields, and volatile crude oil prices. Major names including Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, and Infosys are among those caught in the broader market downturn. This trend reflects a significant cooling in investor sentiment across mid-cap and large-cap segments.
why_it_matters: Portfolio values may see deeper drawdowns as broad selling continues.

headline: Accenture earnings trigger rally in Indian IT ADRs
hook: Indian IT stocks set for a boost
summary: Accenture's latest financial results triggered a strong positive reaction for Indian IT companies. As Accenture is a global industry bellwether, its performance heavily influences sentiment for Indian tech exporters. Indian retail investors can expect this positive momentum to reflect in domestic IT stock prices.
why_it_matters: Expect a short-term rally in domestic IT stocks.

headline: Infosys submits depository participant compliance certificate to exchanges
hook: Routine compliance filing from India's second largest IT firm
summary: Infosys Limited has submitted its compliance certificate required under Regulation 74(5) of the SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018. This routine procedural filing confirms the dematerialisation of securities for the relevant period. Such compliance documents are submitted periodically by all listed companies to stock exchanges. For Indian retail investors, this is standard administrative housekeeping with no impact on stock price or business fundamentals.
why_it_matters: Purely procedural compliance filing with zero impact on stock valuations.
